title: Negative numbers
subtitle: Compare them, move on a number line, and calculate with them.

explanation.title: Negative numbers are below zero
paragraphs: A temperature of −2°C is 2 degrees below zero.
A temperature of −7°C is 7 degrees below zero.
The further below zero the temperature is, the colder it is. So −7°C is colder than −2°C.
On a number line, numbers increase as you move right and decrease as you move left.
That is why −7 is smaller than −2.

comparison.title: Which number is greater?
comparison.intro: Choose > or <. The number further right on the number line is greater.

questions.explanation: −5 is further left than −3, so −5 is smaller.
−2 is left of zero. 1 is right of zero. So −2 is smaller.
0 is to the right of −4, so 0 is greater.
−7 is to the right of −10, so −7 is greater.
−1 is closer to zero and sits to the right of −8, so −1 is greater.
−6 is left of zero. 6 is right of zero. So −6 is smaller.

interactive.title: Move on the number line
interactive.intro: Drag the counter. Moving right makes the number greater. Moving left makes the number smaller.

sign_interactive.title: What do the signs change?
sign_interactive.intro: Tap one sign at a time. For addition and subtraction, watch which way you move. For multiplication and division, watch whether the answer is positive or negative.

method.title: Add and subtract on a number line
method.intro: Use four steps: Understand → Start → Move → Read.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: Decide which way the second number makes you move. Adding a positive moves right. Subtracting a positive moves left. Adding a negative moves left. Subtracting a negative moves right.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Find the first number on the number line. In 5 − (−3), start at 5.

steps.title: Move
steps.text: Subtracting −3 means reverse a move of 3 to the left. Move 3 places right instead.

steps.title: Read
steps.text: Read the number you land on. You land on 8, so 5 − (−3) = 8.

worked_examples.title: Work out −3 + 7
steps: Start at −3 on the number line.
You are adding positive 7, so move 7 places right.
Count through zero and stop at 4.

worked_examples.title: Work out 5 − (−3)
steps: Start at 5 on the number line.
A negative 3 points left.
Subtracting reverses that direction, so move 3 places right.
You land on 8. This is why 5 − (−3) has the same result as 5 + 3.

worked_examples.title: Work out −6 × (−4)
steps: First find the size of the answer: 6 × 4 = 24.
Each negative sign reverses the sign of the answer.
There are two negative signs, so the sign is reversed twice.
Two reversals return to positive, so the answer is 24.

worked_examples.title: Work out 24 ÷ (−3)
steps: First find the size of the answer: 24 ÷ 3 = 8.
There is one negative sign.
One negative reverses the sign of the answer.
So the answer is −8.

worked_examples.title: Work out 3r − q when r = −3 and q = 2
steps: Replace r with −3 and q with 2: 3 × (−3) − 2.
Multiply first. One negative gives a negative answer, so 3 × (−3) = −9.
The calculation is now −9 − 2.
Start at −9 and move 2 places left. You land on −11.

question_bank.title: Practise negative numbers
question_bank.intro: Begin by comparing negative numbers. Then practise moving on a number line, calculating with signs, and using negative values in algebra.
